## 11. New columns, filled missing values, and the files `raw` and `holdout`

This last section works on **`full`** (all the rows: `raw` and `holdout` together, every row has the label `.part`). Doing the work on `full` gives `raw` and `holdout` **exactly the same** values. **Run it after the EDA** (sections 4-10): the EDA was done on `raw` with its missing values.

1.  **11-1** fill the missing values (ONE method);
2.  **11-2** (optional) make new columns;
3.  **11-3** (optional) make time-series features;
4.  **11-4** cut `raw` and `holdout` out of `full` again and **save** the two files (the analysis template reads them).

**Why this does not use the holdout:** the time methods of the fill only look at rows **before** the row (for a holdout row: `raw` and the earlier days of the holdout, which is what you know at that time); `"all"` learns its number on the `raw` rows only; a new column is computed from the row itself; the time-series features use only the past. **Never use `TARGET` to make a predictor** (except its past values in 11-3). The only small look-aheads stay **inside `raw`** (never the holdout): the first time unit of `"time_window"` uses the first `FIRST_K` raw values, and the fallback `"overall"` uses the overall value of the raw rows.

### 11-1. Fill the missing values

A model cannot use a row that has a missing value. They are filled with ONE method, in the table `full`. The outcome (`TARGET`) is never filled. Choose the method in the chunk (`METHOD`); with no time column only `"all"` is possible.

```{r fill-all}
df       <- full                                    # the code below works on a table called df
if (HAS_TIME) df <- df[order(df[[TIME]]), ]         # sorted by time (the time methods need it)
raw_rows <- which(df$.part == "raw")                # the rows of raw: "all" learns its number on them only
df_mean  <- df

# ===== How to fill the missing values (choose here) =====
METHOD      <- "time_window"   # "all" | "expanding" | "time_window" | "last_k" | "same_time"
WINDOW_DAYS <- 30              # for "time_window": how many past time units (days) it looks back at the end (30 = the past 30 days). The rule is written above the time_window code
FIRST_K     <- 10              # for "time_window": the first time unit has no past, so it uses the first FIRST_K observed values of the raw rows (a small look-ahead, only for that unit)
K           <- 10              # for "last_k": use the last K observed values
FALLBACK    <- "overall"       # when there is still nothing to use: "overall" (the overall mean / most common value of the raw rows) | "none"
SAME_WEEKDAY <- TRUE           # "expanding": TRUE = only use the rows with the SAME weekday as this row (weekdays often behave alike)
UNIT        <- "day"           # "week" | "day" | "hour"      the unit of time
if (!HAS_TIME) METHOD <- "all" # no time column: only "all" is possible

# METHOD: which observed values of the same column are used to fill a missing value
#   "all"         : every observed value of the RAW rows (the number is learned on raw only; the holdout gets the same number).
#   "expanding"   : all observed values BEFORE this row's time        (everything known so far)
#   "time_window" : the first time unit has no past                 = the mean of the first FIRST_K observed values of the column
#                   time unit 2 up to WINDOW_DAYS                   = the mean of ALL the observed values before this row's time
#                   after that                                      = the mean of the observed values of the past WINDOW_DAYS time units only
#                   (the exact rule, with an example, is written above the time_window code below)
#   "last_k"      : the last K observed values before this row        (rows are sorted by time)
#   "same_time"   : the other rows with the SAME time as this row     (a cross-section; use it only if they are known at the same moment)
# The four time methods need the table to be sorted by time (it is). They only use OBSERVED values: a filled value never fills another one.
# FALLBACK: if there is still nothing to use (for example the whole window is missing), "overall" uses the overall mean (categorical: the most
#           common value) of the RAW rows (a small look-ahead inside raw, never the holdout), "none" leaves the value missing.
#
# Numeric columns are filled with the MEAN. For the MEDIAN, change  mean(  to  median(  in the lines marked  <-- mean.
# Categorical columns are filled with the most common value.

# most_common(x) returns the most frequent value of x (a function is a saved recipe)
most_common <- function(x) {
  counts <- table(x)
  names(counts)[which.max(counts)]
}

# overall_of(x): the observed values of the RAW rows (the fallback uses their mean / most common value)
overall_of <- function(x) {
  v <- x[raw_rows]
  v[!is.na(v)]
}

if (METHOD != "all") {
  t0 <- lubridate::floor_date(min(df[[TIME]]), UNIT, week_start = 1)               # the start of the first week (Monday) / day / hour
  tm <- floor(as.numeric(difftime(df[[TIME]], t0, units = paste0(UNIT, "s"))))     # whole weeks / days / hours since then
  wd <- format(df[[TIME]], "%u")                                                   # weekday number: Monday = 1 ... Sunday = 7
}

# ---------- METHOD = "all": every observed value of RAW ----------
if (METHOD == "all") {
  for (col in NUM) df_mean[[col]][is.na(df[[col]])] <- mean(df[[col]][raw_rows], na.rm = TRUE)     # <-- mean
  for (col in CAT) df_mean[[col]][is.na(df[[col]])] <- most_common(df[[col]][raw_rows])
}

# ---------- METHOD = "expanding": observed values before this row's time ----------
if (METHOD == "expanding") {
  for (col in c(NUM, CAT)) {
    x <- df[[col]]                                   # the ORIGINAL values: filled values are never used to fill other rows
    for (i in which(is.na(x))) {                     # every row where this column is missing
      ok <- tm < tm[i]                               # rows before this row's time
      if (SAME_WEEKDAY) ok <- ok & wd == wd[i]       # ... and only the rows with the same weekday
      pool <- x[ok]                                  # their values
      pool <- pool[!is.na(pool)]                     # only observed values
      if (length(pool) == 0 && FALLBACK == "overall") pool <- overall_of(x)   # nothing in the past: the overall value of raw
      if (length(pool) > 0 &&  is.numeric(x)) df_mean[[col]][i] <- mean(pool)                  # <-- mean
      if (length(pool) > 0 && !is.numeric(x)) df_mean[[col]][i] <- most_common(pool)
    }
  }
}

# ---------- METHOD = "time_window": how a missing value is filled (example: WINDOW_DAYS = 30, UNIT = "day") ----------
# A missing value is filled with the MEAN (numeric column) or the most common value (categorical column) of the OBSERVED values of the same column:
#   - day 1 (the first time unit) has no past: the first FIRST_K (10) observed values of the column are used;
#   - day 2 up to day 30: all the observed values before this day are used (the whole past so far);
#   - day 31 and later: only the observed values of the past 30 days are used (the 30 days right before this day);
#   - if there is still nothing to use (for example the past 30 days are all missing): the overall mean of the raw rows is used (FALLBACK = "overall").
# Only really observed values are used: a filled value never fills another one.
if (METHOD == "time_window") {
  for (col in c(NUM, CAT)) {
    x       <- df[[col]]
    x_raw   <- x[raw_rows]
    first_k <- head(x_raw[!is.na(x_raw)], FIRST_K)                                  # the first FIRST_K observed values of the raw rows
    for (i in which(is.na(x))) {
      if (tm[i] == 0) {                                                             # the first time unit: there is no past
        pool <- first_k
      } else if (tm[i] < WINDOW_DAYS) {                                             # time unit 2 up to WINDOW_DAYS: all the observed values before this row's time
        pool <- x[tm < tm[i]]
      } else {                                                                      # after that: only the observed values of the past WINDOW_DAYS time units
        pool <- x[tm < tm[i] & tm >= tm[i] - WINDOW_DAYS]
      }
      pool <- pool[!is.na(pool)]                                                    # only observed values
      if (length(pool) == 0 && FALLBACK == "overall") pool <- overall_of(x)         # still nothing: the overall value of raw
      if (length(pool) > 0 &&  is.numeric(x)) df_mean[[col]][i] <- mean(pool)                  # <-- mean
      if (length(pool) > 0 && !is.numeric(x)) df_mean[[col]][i] <- most_common(pool)
    }
  }
}

# ---------- METHOD = "last_k": the last K observed values before this row ----------
if (METHOD == "last_k") {
  for (col in c(NUM, CAT)) {
    x <- df[[col]]
    for (i in which(is.na(x))) {
      past <- x[seq_len(i - 1)]                      # all rows before this row (rows are sorted by time), 1:(i-1)
      past <- past[!is.na(past)]                     # only observed values
      pool <- tail(past, K)                          # the last K of them
      if (length(pool) == 0 && FALLBACK == "overall") pool <- overall_of(x)   # nothing to use: the overall value of raw
      if (length(pool) > 0 &&  is.numeric(x)) df_mean[[col]][i] <- mean(pool)                  # <-- mean
      if (length(pool) > 0 && !is.numeric(x)) df_mean[[col]][i] <- most_common(pool)
    }
  }
}

# ---------- METHOD = "same_time": the other rows with the same time ----------
if (METHOD == "same_time") {
  for (col in c(NUM, CAT)) {
    x <- df[[col]]
    for (i in which(is.na(x))) {
      pool <- x[tm == tm[i] & seq_along(x) != i]     # the other rows with the same time
      pool <- pool[!is.na(pool)]
      if (length(pool) == 0 && FALLBACK == "overall") pool <- overall_of(x)   # nothing to use: the overall value of raw
      if (length(pool) > 0 &&  is.numeric(x)) df_mean[[col]][i] <- mean(pool)                  # <-- mean
      if (length(pool) > 0 && !is.numeric(x)) df_mean[[col]][i] <- most_common(pool)
    }
  }
}

# How many values were missing before, and how many are still missing (only possible with FALLBACK = "none")
data.frame(missing_before = colSums(is.na(df[c(NUM, CAT)])),
           still_missing  = colSums(is.na(df_mean[c(NUM, CAT)])))

full <- df_mean                                     # ALL the rows, filled with the same method
```

### 11-2. (Optional) Make new columns

Copy the lines you need and edit the names. The new columns are made on `full`, so `raw` and `holdout` both get them. They are made **after** the fill, from filled columns.

- Use only rules that look at **one row**, or numbers **you write** (a cut-off of 15 degrees). A number learned from the data (a mean, a median, a quantile) would also use the holdout.
- **Never use the target (`TARGET`) to make a predictor.**
- The last lines of the chunk write the new names in `NUM` / `CAT`: **edit `new_num` and `new_cat`** (only the columns you kept).

```{r new-columns}
WEEK_ORDER <- c("Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday")

# --- a number from a date: how many days the station has been open on that day
full$station_age_days <- as.numeric(full$date - full$opened_date)

# --- parts of a date (categories)
full$weekday <- factor(WEEK_ORDER[as.numeric(format(full$date, "%u"))], levels = WEEK_ORDER)     # Monday ... Sunday
full$month   <- factor(format(full$date, "%m"))                                                   # "03" ... "09"   (as a number instead: as.numeric(format(full$date, "%m")))

# --- two columns together
full$feels_diff <- full$feels_like_c - full$temp_c                    # a difference
full$wind_rain  <- full$wind_kmh * full$rain_mm                       # a product

# --- one column changed
full$temp_c2  <- full$temp_c^2                                         # squared
full$log_rain <- log(full$rain_mm + 1)                                 # log (+ 1 because rain_mm can be 0)

# --- a rule that you write (the cut-offs are YOUR numbers, not learned from the data)
full$is_rainy  <- as.integer(full$rain_mm > 0)                                                                    # 0 / 1
full$temp_band <- cut(full$temp_c, breaks = c(-Inf, 5, 15, 25, Inf), labels = c("cold", "cool", "warm", "hot"))   # a category

# --- two categories together
full$type_charging <- paste(full$station_type, full$has_charging, sep = "_")

# ===== Tell the template about the new columns (EDIT: only the columns you kept) =====
new_num <- character(0)      # the numeric columns you made, for example c("station_age_days", "temp_c2")
new_cat <- character(0)      # the category columns you made, for example c("weekday", "temp_band")

NUM <- unique(c(NUM, new_num))        # for the analysis template (saved in 11-4)
CAT <- unique(c(CAT, new_cat))

sapply(full[c(new_num, new_cat)], function(x) class(x)[1])
sapply(full[c(new_num, new_cat)], function(x) sum(is.na(x)))     # missing values of the new columns
```

### 11-3. (Optional) Time-series features of the target

**Optional: lagged features are for later**, if the models do not work well enough without them. Only if the data has a time column and the target is a number that follows the time (a series). Set `TS_MODE` in the settings: `"none"` (the default), `"row"` or `"bar"`. Every feature uses **only the past** of the row (the previous rows or bars), and it is made on `full`, so the first holdout rows have their history. The first `LONG` rows (bars) have no full history: they are dropped.

- `"row"`: from the previous **rows** (lags 1-3, mean and sd of the previous 5 and 20 rows). For data with ONE row per time point (a price series). With several rows per day (the stations of the bike data) the previous row is another station: do not use it there.
- `"bar"`: from the previous **days / hours**: one value per bar (the mean of the target over the rows of the bar), then lags and rolling mean / sd of those values. Use it when there are several rows per day. In the chunk keep ONE of the three lines that define the bars (hour / day / week).
- The names (`ret_lag1` ... `sharpe_short`) come from finance: read `ret` as "the target". The new columns are added to `NUM`.

#### Based on rows (`TS_MODE <- "row"`)

```{r time-series-features}
if (TS_MODE == "row") {
  # ===== Time-series feature engineering =====  
  SHORT <- 5
  LONG  <- 20

  y <- full[[TARGET]]
  n <- nrow(full)

  # 1. Lag features
  full$ret_lag1 <- dplyr::lag(y, 1)
  full$ret_lag2 <- dplyr::lag(y, 2)
  full$ret_lag3 <- dplyr::lag(y, 3)

  # Absolute size of the previous observation
  full$ret_abs_lag1 <- abs(full$ret_lag1)

  # 2. Rolling mean and standard deviation of past values
  ret_mean_short <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  ret_sd_short   <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  ret_sd_long    <- rep(NA_real_, n)

  for (i in (SHORT + 1):n) {
    past <- y[(i - SHORT):(i - 1)]
    ret_mean_short[i] <- mean(past)
    ret_sd_short[i]   <- sd(past)
  }

  for (i in (LONG + 1):n) {
    ret_sd_long[i] <- sd(y[(i - LONG):(i - 1)])
  }

  full$ret_mean_short <- ret_mean_short
  full$ret_sd_short   <- ret_sd_short
  full$ret_sd_long    <- ret_sd_long

  # 3. Sharpe-like ratio
  full$sharpe_short <- ifelse(
    full$ret_sd_short > 0,
    full$ret_mean_short / full$ret_sd_short,
    NA_real_
  )

  # 4. Drop initial rows without a full history
  new_cols <- c(
    "ret_lag1", "ret_lag2", "ret_lag3", "ret_abs_lag1",
    "ret_mean_short", "ret_sd_short", "ret_sd_long",
    "sharpe_short"
  )

  cat("Rows before:", nrow(full), "| Dropped:", LONG, "\n")

  full <- full[seq_len(n) > LONG, ]

  # Add new features to numeric predictors (unique(): running the chunk again does not add the names twice)
  NUM <- unique(c(NUM, new_cols))        # the new columns become numeric predictors (unique(): no repeated names)

  # Check remaining missing values
  colSums(is.na(full[new_cols]))
}
```

#### Based on a unit of time, day or hour (`TS_MODE <- "bar"`)

```{r time-series-bars}
if (TS_MODE == "bar") {
  # ===== Time-series features by TIME BAR (hour / day / week): every feature uses ONLY the previous bars =====
  SHORT <- 5            # the short window: the previous 5 bars
  LONG  <- 20           # the long window: the previous 20 bars

  # Which bar (week / day / hour) does every row belong to? Keep ONE of the three lines.
  tm <- floor(as.numeric(difftime(full[[TIME]], lubridate::floor_date(min(full[[TIME]]), "hour"), units = "hours")))     # hour bars
  # tm <- floor(as.numeric(difftime(full[[TIME]], lubridate::floor_date(min(full[[TIME]]), "day"), units = "days")))     # day bars
  # tm <- floor(as.numeric(difftime(full[[TIME]], lubridate::floor_date(min(full[[TIME]]), "week", week_start = 1), units = "weeks")))   # week bars

  # Renumber the bars: only the bars that HAVE rows count. Weekends, holidays and nights without data are skipped,
  # so "the previous bar" is the previous bar WITH data (Monday -> Friday if there is no weekend data, Monday -> Sunday if there is).
  tm <- match(tm, sort(unique(tm))) - 1

  y <- full[[TARGET]]     # the series (for returns: the return column)

  # 1) One value per bar: the mean of the series inside the bar (use sum(...) instead of mean(...) if the values add up)
  nb <- max(tm) + 1                                        # number of bars (bar numbers start at 0, R positions at 1)
  bar_value <- rep(NA_real_, nb)
  bar_mean  <- tapply(y, tm, mean)                         # mean of every bar (names = bar numbers)
  bar_value[as.numeric(names(bar_mean)) + 1] <- bar_mean   # +1: bar number 0 is position 1

  # 2) Features of every bar, from the PREVIOUS bars only (the bar itself is NOT included)
  f_lag1 <- dplyr::lag(bar_value, 1)                       # the previous bar
  f_lag2 <- dplyr::lag(bar_value, 2)
  f_lag3 <- dplyr::lag(bar_value, 3)
  f_mean_short <- rep(NA_real_, nb)
  f_sd_short   <- rep(NA_real_, nb)
  f_sd_long    <- rep(NA_real_, nb)
  for (b in (SHORT + 1):nb) {
    past <- bar_value[(b - SHORT):(b - 1)]                 # the previous SHORT bars
    past <- past[!is.na(past)]
    if (length(past) >= 1) f_mean_short[b] <- mean(past)
    if (length(past) >= 2) f_sd_short[b]   <- sd(past)
  }
  for (b in (LONG + 1):nb) {
    past <- bar_value[(b - LONG):(b - 1)]
    past <- past[!is.na(past)]
    if (length(past) >= 2) f_sd_long[b] <- sd(past)
  }

  # 3) Give every ROW the features of its bar
  pos <- tm + 1                                            # the position of the row's bar
  full$ret_lag1       <- f_lag1[pos]
  full$ret_lag2       <- f_lag2[pos]
  full$ret_lag3       <- f_lag3[pos]
  full$ret_mean_short <- f_mean_short[pos]
  full$ret_sd_short   <- f_sd_short[pos]
  full$ret_sd_long    <- f_sd_long[pos]
  full$sharpe_short   <- ifelse(full$ret_sd_short > 0, full$ret_mean_short / full$ret_sd_short, NA)

  # 4) Drop the rows of the first LONG bars (no full history)
  new_cols <- c("ret_lag1", "ret_lag2", "ret_lag3", "ret_mean_short", "ret_sd_short", "ret_sd_long", "sharpe_short")
  cat("rows before:", nrow(full), "| dropped (first", LONG, "bars):", sum(tm < LONG), "\n")
  full <- full[tm >= LONG, ]
  NUM <- unique(c(NUM, new_cols))        # the new columns become numeric predictors (unique(): no repeated names)
  colSums(is.na(full[new_cols]))        
}
```

### 11-4. Cut `raw` and `holdout` out of `full` and save them

```{r save-raw-holdout}
raw     <- full[full$.part == "raw",     names(full) != ".part"]
holdout <- full[full$.part == "holdout", names(full) != ".part"]
full    <- full[names(full) != ".part"]                    # full = raw followed by holdout, without the label
df      <- raw                                             # the working copy of the EDA: the same as raw

saveRDS(raw,     "raw.rds")                                # the analysis template reads these three files
saveRDS(holdout, "holdout.rds")
saveRDS(list(NUM = NUM, CAT = CAT), "roles.rds")           # which columns are numeric / categorical predictors

cat("saved: raw", nrow(raw), "rows | holdout", nrow(holdout), "rows | numeric predictors", length(NUM), "| categorical predictors", length(CAT), "\n")
cat("missing values left in the predictors: raw", sum(is.na(raw[c(NUM, CAT)])), "| holdout", sum(is.na(holdout[c(NUM, CAT)])), "\n")
```

## Appendix: basic operations (the original "section 0" reference)

Every chunk below is independent of your data: it uses a tiny table `ex`. Operations that change something are done on a copy (`temp <- ex`), and in R **a copy never changes the original**.

```{r appendix-example}
ex <- data.frame(customer_id = c(1, 2, 3), age = c(25, 40, 31), gender = c("F", "M", "F"))
ex
```

### Vector (a pandas Series: one column of values)

```{r appendix-vector}
# ===== Add to a vector =====
s <- c(25, 40, 31)
s <- c(s, 50)                       # add at the end
s <- c(10, s)                       # add at the front
s <- append(s, 99, after = 2)       # add after the 2nd element
s

# ===== Remove from a vector =====
s <- c(25, 40, 31, 40, 50)
s[-1]                               # remove the 1st element (by position)
s[-c(1, 3)]                         # remove the 1st and the 3rd
s[s != 40]                          # remove every element equal to 40 (by value)
s[!(s %in% c(40, 50))]              # remove several values at once
setdiff(s, 40)                      # remove a value and the repeated values (the result has no repeats)
# DANGER: s[-which(s == 99)] returns NOTHING when no element equals 99. Use the lines above instead.

# ===== The same with names (the list of variables) =====
cols <- c("n_items", "n_units", "age", "tenure_days", "gender")
cols <- c(cols, "ret_lag1")                  # add a variable
cols <- unique(c(cols, "ret_lag1"))          # add it again: unique() keeps it only once
cols <- setdiff(cols, "age")                 # remove a variable
cols <- cols[!cols %in% c("n_units", "gender")]     # remove several variables
cols
"age" %in% cols                      # is it in the vector?  TRUE / FALSE
which(cols == "tenure_days")         # at which position?
length(cols)                         # how many?

# ===== Named vector: remove or change by name =====
s <- c(a = 25, b = 40, c = 31)
s[names(s) != "b"]                   # remove the element named b
s[!names(s) %in% c("a", "c")]        # remove several by name
s["b"] <- 41                         # change one value
s["d"] <- 60                         # add a new named element
s

# ===== Change, sort, repeat =====
s <- c(25, 40, 31, 40)
s[2] <- 0                            # change the 2nd element
sort(s); sort(s, decreasing = TRUE)  # sort
rev(s)                               # reverse the order
unique(s)                            # remove the repeated values
duplicated(s)                        # TRUE for the repeated ones
head(s, 2); tail(s, 2)               # the first 2 / the last 2                              # the names
```

### Data frame (a pandas DataFrame: several columns)

```{r appendix-dataframe}
d1 <- data.frame(age = c(25, 40, 31), gender = c("F", "M", "F"))    # {column = values}
d2 <- tibble(age = c(25, 40, 31), gender = c("F", "M", "F"))        # tibble: a data frame that prints nicely
d3 <- tribble(~age, ~gender,                                        # row by row
              25, "F",
              40, "M")
d4 <- bind_rows(list(age = 25, gender = "F"), list(age = 40, gender = "M"))   # a list of rows
d1; d2; d3; d4
# d5 <- read_csv("file.csv")                                         # from a file (see section 1)

# Taking ONE column out of a table
ex$age                      # a vector (like a Series)
ex[["age"]]                 # the same
pull(ex, age)               # the same
ex["age"]                   # still a table with one column
select(ex, age)             # still a table with one column
```

### Select columns

```{r appendix-select}
select(ex, age, gender)                        # by name
ex[c("age", "gender")]                         # same, base R
temp <- select(ex, age, gender)                # keep the result in a new table
select(ex, -gender)                            # everything except gender
select(ex, 1, 3)                               # by position: 1st and 3rd column
select(ex, where(is.numeric))                  # by type: numeric columns
select(ex, where(is.character))                # text columns   (also is.factor, is.logical)
# select(df, where(is.Date))                   # date columns: needs library(lubridate)
select(ex, contains("age"))                    # name contains "age"
select(ex, starts_with("cust"))                # name starts with "cust"   (also ends_with)

cols <- setdiff(names(ex), c("customer_id"))   # a list of names: all columns except customer_id
ex[cols]                                       # select with that list
select(ex, all_of(cols))                       # same
names(ex)[str_starts(names(ex), "a")]          # column names that start with "a"
```

### Rename columns

```{r appendix-rename}
rename(ex, customer_age = age, sex = gender)   # rename(NEW = OLD)  <- the new name comes first

temp <- ex
names(temp) <- c("a", "b", "c")                # replace all names (same number, same order)
temp

rename_with(ex, toupper)                       # apply a function to every name, to upper case
rename_with(ex, ~ str_replace_all(str_to_lower(str_trim(.x)), " ", "_"))   # rule: trim spaces, lower case, " " -> "_"
rename_with(ex, ~ paste0("c_", .x))            # add a prefix to every column
rename_with(ex, ~ paste0(.x, "_raw"))          # add a suffix to every column
```

### Change the column order

```{r appendix-reorder}
select(ex, gender, age)                        # list them in the new order (only the listed columns are kept)
relocate(ex, gender)                           # move gender to the front, keep the others
relocate(ex, gender, .after = age)             # put gender right after age
select(ex, gender, everything())               # gender first, then all the others
```

### Add and delete columns

```{r appendix-add-delete}
temp <- ex
temp$age2  <- temp$age * 2                          # a new column from a calculation
temp$flag  <- 0                                     # the same value in every row
temp$group <- ifelse(temp$age >= 30, "old", "young")   # value by condition (like np.where)
temp
temp <- mutate(temp, age3 = age * 3)                # the same with mutate
temp <- select(temp, -age2, -flag)                  # delete columns
temp$age3 <- NULL                                   # delete one column
group_col <- temp$group                             # take a column out ...
temp$group <- NULL                                  # ... and delete it (like pandas pop)
temp
```

### Change column types

```{r appendix-types}
temp <- ex
temp$age    <- as.numeric(temp$age)                 # also as.integer, as.character
temp$gender <- as.factor(temp$gender)               # category
temp$d <- c("2024-01-05", "2024-02-10", "bad")
temp$d <- as.Date(temp$d, format = "%Y-%m-%d")      # text -> date; "bad" becomes NA  or temp$d[temp$d == "bad"] <- NA
temp
sapply(temp, class)
```

### Select rows

```{r appendix-rows}
ex[ex$age > 30, ]                              # by condition (base R)
filter(ex, age > 30)                           # by condition (dplyr; rows with NA in the condition are dropped)
ex[ex$age > 30, c("age", "gender")]            # condition + columns
filter(ex, age > 30) %>% select(age, gender)   # same
head(ex, 2)                                    # first 2 rows
ex[1:2, 1:2]                                   # by position
slice(ex, 1:2)                                 # same
slice_sample(ex, n = 2)                        # 2 random rows (run set.seed(0) first to get the same rows every time)
slice(ex, 2:n())                               # from the 2nd row to the end
```

### Delete rows

```{r appendix-delete-rows}
ex[-c(1, 3), ]                                 # delete rows 1 and 3 by position
slice(ex, -c(1, 3))                            # same
filter(ex, !(age > 120))                       # delete rows by condition (= keep the others)
ex[ex$age <= 120, ]                            # same, base R
# DANGER: ex[-which(ex$age > 120), ] returns ZERO rows when no row matches. Use the lines above instead.
```

### Row names ("index")

```{r appendix-index}
# A tibble has no index: keep the ID as an ordinary column. For a plain data.frame you can use row names:
temp <- as.data.frame(ex)
temp <- column_to_rownames(temp, "customer_id")      # column -> row names     (pandas set_index)
temp
temp <- rownames_to_column(temp, "customer_id")      # row names -> column     (pandas reset_index)
temp
```

### Flip row and column

```{r flip}
temp <- as.data.frame(t(temp))
temp
```

### Select text by pattern

```{r appendix-strings}
x <- c("Mouse", "Laptop", "Keyboard", "Monitor", "Headphones")
str_starts(x, "M")               # starts with M
str_ends(x, "er")                # ends with "er"
str_detect(x, "ou")              # contains "ou" anywhere
str_detect(x, "^(M|L)")          # starts with M or L
x[str_starts(x, "M")]            # the matching values themselves
```

## Date and time

```{r date-time}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

d <- as.Date("2024-03-05")                          # date (Tuesday)
x <- as.POSIXct("2024-03-05 14:07:09", tz = "UTC")  # date + time

# ===== Current date and time =====
Sys.Date()       # current date
Sys.time()       # current date and time

# ===== Date/time -> text =====
format(x, "%Y")       # year: "2024"     %y : "24"
format(x, "%m")       # month: "03"
format(x, "%d")       # day: "05"
format(x, "%H")       # hour: "14"
format(x, "%M")       # minute: "07"
format(x, "%S")       # second: "09"
format(x, "%u")       # weekday: Monday = 1, Sunday = 7
format(x, "%w")       # weekday: Sunday = 0, Saturday = 6
format(x, "%Y-%m")    # year-month: "2024-03"
weekdays(d)           # weekday name: "Tuesday"
months(d)             # month name: "March"

# ===== Text -> date or date-time =====
as.Date("2024-03-05")
as.Date("05/03/2024", format = "%d/%m/%Y")

as.POSIXct("2024-03-05 14:07:09",
           format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", tz = "UTC")

# Parse dates with lubridate
ymd("2024-03-05")
mdy("03/05/2024")
dmy("05/03/2024")
ymd_hms("2024-03-05 14:07:09")

# ===== Extract date components =====
year(d)
month(d)
day(d)
wday(d, label = TRUE, week_start = 1)
yday(d)       # day of the year
week(d)
quarter(d)

# ===== Date arithmetic =====
d - 30                                  # 30 days before
as.Date("2024-04-01") - d               # days between dates
x - 7                                   # 7 seconds before
x - days(7)                             # 7 days before
difftime(x, as.POSIXct("2024-03-05 08:00:00", tz = "UTC"),
         units = "hours")               # hours between dates
d %m-% months(1)                        # 1 month before

# ===== Round down or up to a period =====
floor_date(d, "week", week_start = 1)   # Monday of that week
floor_date(x, "day")                    # start of the day
floor_date(x, "hour")                   # start of the hour
floor_date(d, "month")                  # first day of the month
ceiling_date(d, "month")                # start of the next month

# ===== Create date sequences =====
seq(as.Date("2024-03-01"), as.Date("2024-03-05"), by = "day")
seq(as.Date("2024-01-01"), as.Date("2024-12-01"), by = "month")

# ===== Date-time -> date =====
as.Date(x)                              # remove time of day
```
